conversation.content: 帮我系统分析一下英伟达这家公司的投资价值，我主要关心数据中心业务的盈利能力，最后我想自己用财报数据算一算。

好。英伟达现在的核心叙事几乎可以浓缩成一句话：数据中心 GPU。逻辑链条是——大模型训练和推理需求爆发，H100/H200 这类高端加速卡供不应求，于是数据中心分部的营收占比从过去的‘一半左右’迅速飙到八成以上，成了绝对大头；同时因为卖的是高附加值芯片加软件生态（CUDA、NVLink），整体毛利率被拉到历史高位。投资价值的多空分歧基本都围绕这条链：多头赌需求持续、护城河（CUDA 生态）够深；空头担心客户集中（几家云厂商占大头）、竞品追赶（AMD MI300、各家自研 ASIC）以及周期性。我们先把盈利能力的数字坐实，再谈估值。
毛利率被拉到历史高位，大概是多高的水平？
在数据中心高端芯片的拉动下，公司整体毛利率一度冲到 70% 多的区间，明显高于过去以游戏显卡为主、毛利率 60% 出头的时代。这个跃升不是靠降本，而是产品结构变了——卖的东西单价和附加值都上了一个台阶。但要提醒：这么高的毛利率本身就是供需极度紧张的产物，能不能维持，取决于这种紧张还能持续多久，一旦供给跟上或需求降温，毛利率回归是大概率事件，所以做模型时不能简单线性外推。
那按现在的盈利，估值算贵吗？
取决于你用什么锚。看静态 PE 确实不低，市场已经把高增长预期打进去了；但如果数据中心营收还能维持高速增长，forward PE 会被未来盈利摊薄，看起来就没那么离谱。关键变量始终是数据中心这块营收能不能持续放量——它既是营收大头，又是毛利率的支撑，一荣俱荣、一损俱损。所以与其纠结当前 PE，不如把精力放在跟踪数据中心营收的环比趋势和大客户的采购指引上。
我最担心的就是周期性。万一 AI 资本开支退潮呢？
这是最大的尾部风险，而且是‘双杀’式的。一旦云厂商和大企业开始收缩 AI 相关的 capex，数据中心营收会掉，产能利用率下来后毛利率也会跟着回落，营收和利润率同时下滑、估值再被下修，就是典型的戴维斯双杀。所以对英伟达来说，盯紧几家大客户（微软、谷歌、Meta、亚马逊）的资本开支指引，往往比盯英伟达自己上个季度的财报还重要——客户的开支计划是领先指标，财报是滞后结果。
竞争格局你怎么看？AMD 的 MI300 和云厂商自研 ASIC 到底能不能撼动它？

分两个层面看。硬件层面，AMD MI300、谷歌 TPU、亚马逊 Trainium/Inferentia 这些在纸面算力和显存上确实在逼近甚至局部超越，大客户也乐意扶持二供来压价、降低单一依赖。但真正的护城河在软件层面——CUDA 生态加上 cuDNN、NCCL、以及一整套被全世界开发者和框架默认适配的工具链，迁移成本极高。自研 ASIC 在自家固定负载上跑得动、性价比好，但通用性和生态差得远，外部客户不会为了省点钱去吃整条工具链不成熟的苦。所以我的判断是：竞品会蚕食‘价格敏感、负载固定’的那部分份额，压制英伟达的定价权和毛利率上限，但短期内难以撼动它在‘通用、前沿、生态依赖’这块的统治地位。对投资来说，要盯的不是‘会不会被取代’，而是‘毛利率会不会因为二供出现而见顶回落’。
那如果只能看一个领先指标来预判它的拐点，你会看哪个？

我会看大客户的资本开支指引，而且是‘指引’不是‘已实现’。原因前面说过：英伟达数据中心营收的需求方高度集中在几家超大云厂商和头部 AI 公司，它们的 capex 计划是英伟达订单的领先指标，通常领先一到两个季度。当这几家在财报电话会里开始把 AI 相关 capex 的措辞从‘加速投入’转成‘优化效率/趋于理性’，往往就是需求降温的早期信号，会先于英伟达自己的营收下滑体现出来。第二个辅助指标是交付周期/缺货程度，从‘一卡难求’变成‘随时能买到’，意味着供需拐点到了，毛利率随后承压。把这两个盯住，比逐季抠英伟达自己的财报更能提前判断。
客户集中这个风险我老板很在意，能具体讲讲它怎么传导成投资风险吗？

客户集中的风险本质是‘议价权和需求稳定性都押在少数人身上’。具体有三条传导路径：第一，议价权——当你大部分数据中心营收来自四五家超大云厂商，它们联合压价或扶持二供（AMD、自研芯片）的能力就很强，会直接侵蚀你引以为傲的高毛利率，这是对盈利质量的慢性侵蚀；第二，需求同步性——这几家的 AI capex 周期高度相关，一旦宏观或行业逻辑变化，它们很可能同时踩刹车，需求不是平滑下滑而是断崖，营收波动被放大；第三，库存与预付——景气时客户为锁产能会下大额预付/长单，一旦需求转向，这些会变成砍单和库存减值的来源，财报上突然计提。所以分析时不能只看英伟达自己多强，要把这几家大客户的财务健康、capex 指引、以及它们自研替代的进度当成英伟达的‘表外风险敞口’来跟踪。这也是为什么我一直强调盯客户指引。
软件生态是护城河我认同，但护城河也可能被绕过。有没有什么信号能提前看出 CUDA 的锁定在松动？

好问题，护城河不是永久的，要盯它的‘渗漏点’。几个领先信号：第一，编译器/中间层的成熟度——像 OpenAI Triton、各类把模型从 CUDA 解耦到多后端的编译栈（比如能一键编译到 AMD ROCm 或自研芯片）一旦好用，开发者就不必直接写 CUDA，迁移成本下降；第二，主流框架的多后端支持度——PyTorch 等对非英伟达后端的支持从‘能跑’变成‘性能接近、生产可用’，是关键转折；第三，大客户公开的自研芯片承载比例——当超大云厂商把自家相当比例的推理负载迁到自研 ASIC 并对外背书，说明生态壁垒在它们那里已经被绕过；第四，模型层的标准化——推理引擎（vLLM、TensorRT-LLM 等）抽象掉底层硬件后，用户感知的是引擎而非 CUDA。这些不是一夜之间的事，但任何一个明显加速，都会先反映成英伟达定价权的松动、再反映到毛利率上。所以跟踪护城河，比跟踪单季营收更能预判长期拐点。
估值我还是没底。除了 PE，有没有更适合这种高增长、强周期股的估值思路？

对这种又高增长又强周期的票，单看静态 PE 最容易被‘骗’——景气顶点利润高、PE 看着低，反而是危险信号（周期顶）。更适合的几个角度：第一，看 forward PE 和 PEG，把增长摊进去，但前提是你对未来增速的假设要保守、要做情景分析（牛/中性/熊三档），别用券商最乐观的预期；第二，盯‘量价’而非单看利润——数据中心营收的环比增速、订单/积压、产能利用率这些领先量，比滞后的利润更早反映拐点；第三，做‘正常化盈利’估值：用一个穿越周期的、可持续的毛利率和营收水平去算，而不是用景气顶点的超额利润外推，避免在周期顶给周期股戴上成长股的估值；第四，关注下行保护——极端情况下（capex 退潮）营收和毛利率同时回落时的盈利底在哪，对应的估值是否还能接受。核心心法是：对周期成长股，估值不是算一个精确数字，而是用情景区间和领先指标管理‘买贵了’的风险。这也是为什么我让你先把营收和毛利率这两个实数坐实，再谈估值。
讲得很清楚。那我想用最近一个财年的数据，自己算一下数据中心这块大致的毛利贡献。你帮我把数据中心分部营收和公司整体毛利率从那一页里读出来。
好，我去把那一页里最近财年的数据中心分部营收和公司整体毛利率两个数读出来给你，你拿这两个一乘就能估出数据中心的毛利量级了。
好，麻烦了。

,

, and

AI data center
hardware in the midst of the

and US$5 trillion in

.

19

's "
Magnificent Seven

[
20

History
[
edit
]
Founding
[
edit

, where Nvidia's three co-founders agreed to start the company in late 1992

Nvidia was founded on April 5, 1993,
[
21
]
[
22
]
[
23
]
by Jensen Huang, a
Taiwanese-American
electrical engineer who was previously the director of CoreWare at
LSI Logic
and a
microprocessor
designer at
AMD
;
Chris Malachowsky
, an engineer who worked at
Sun Microsystems
; and
Curtis Priem
, who was previously a senior staff engineer and graphics chip designer at
IBM
and Sun Microsystems.
[
24
]
[
25
]
In late 1992, the three men agreed to start the company in a meeting at a
Denny's
roadside diner on Berryessa Road in East
San Jose
.
[
26
]
[
27
]
[
28
]
[
29
]
At the time, Malachowsky and Priem were frustrated with Sun's management and were looking to leave, but Huang was on "firmer ground",
[
30
]
in that he was already running his own division at LSI.
[
27
]
The three co-founders discussed a vision of the future which was so compelling that Huang decided to leave LSI
[
30
]
and become the chief executive officer of their new startup.
[
27
]
The three co-founders envisioned graphics-based processing as the best trajectory for tackling challenges that had eluded general-purpose computing methods.
[
30
]
As Huang later explained: "We also observed that video games were simultaneously one of the most computationally challenging problems and would have incredibly high sales volume. Those two conditions don't happen very often. Video games was our
killer app
- a flywheel to reach large markets funding huge
R&D
to solve massive computational problems."
[
30
]
The first problem was who would quit first. Huang's wife, Lori, did not want him to resign from LSI unless Malachowsky resigned from Sun at the same time, and Malachowsky's wife, Melody, felt the same way about Huang.
[
31
]
Priem broke that deadlock by resigning first from Sun, effective December 31, 1992.
[
31
]
According to Priem, this put pressure on Huang and Malachowsky to not leave him to "flail alone", so they gave notice too.
[
32
]
Huang left LSI and "officially joined Priem on February 17", which was also Huang's 30th birthday, while Malachowsky left Sun in early March.
[
32
]
In early 1993, the three founders began working together on their new startup in Priem's townhouse in
Fremont, California
.
[
33
]
With $40,000 in the bank (equivalent to $89,000 in 2025), the company was born.
[
30
]
The company subsequently received $20 million of venture capital funding from
Sequoia Capital
,
Sutter Hill Ventures
, and others.
[
34
]
During the late 1990s, Nvidia was one of 70 startup companies pursuing the idea that graphics acceleration for video games was the path to the future.
[
26
]
Only two survived: Nvidia and
ATI Technologies
, the latter of which merged into AMD.
[
26
]
Nvidia initially had no name.
[
35
]
Priem's first idea was "Primal Graphics", a
syllabic abbreviation
of two of the founders' last names, but that left out Huang.
[
35
]
They soon discovered it was impossible to create a workable name with syllables from all three founders' names, after considering "Huaprimal", "Prihuamal", "Malluapri", etc.
[
35
]
The next idea came from Priem's idea for the name of Nvidia's first product.
[
35
]
Priem originally wanted to call it the "GXNV", as in the "next version" of the GX graphics chips which he had worked on at Sun.
[
33
]
Then Huang told Priem to "drop the GX", resulting in the name "NV".
[
33
]
Priem made a list of words with the letters "NV" in them.
[
35
]
At one point, Malachowsky and Priem wanted to call the company NVision, but that name was already taken by a manufacturer of toilet paper.
[
27
]
Both Priem
[
35
]
and Huang have taken credit for coming up with the name Nvidia,
[
27
]
from "
invidia
", the Latin word for "envy".
[
30
]
After the company outgrew Priem's townhouse, its original headquarters office was in
Sunnyvale, California
.
[
30
]
First graphics accelerator
[
edit
]
Nvidia's first graphics accelerator, the
NV1
, was designed to process
quadrilateral
primitives
(
forward texture mapping
), a feature that set it apart from competitors, who preferred triangle primitives.
[
27
]
However, when
Microsoft
introduced the
DirectX
platform, it chose not to support any other graphics software and announced that its
Direct3D
API would exclusively support triangles.
[
27
]
[
36
]
As a result, the NV1 failed to gain traction in the market.
[
37
]
Nvidia had also entered into a partnership with
Sega
to supply the graphics chip for the
Dreamcast
console and worked on the project for about a year. However, Nvidia's technology was already lagging behind competitors. This placed the company in a difficult position: continue working on a chip that was likely doomed to fail or abandon the project, risking financial collapse.
[
38
]
In a pivotal moment, Sega's president,
Shoichiro Irimajiri
, visited Huang in person to inform him that Sega had decided to choose another vendor for the Dreamcast. However, Irimajiri believed in Nvidia's potential and persuaded Sega's management to invest $5 million into the company. Huang later reflected that this funding was all that kept Nvidia afloat, and that Irimajiri's "understanding and generosity gave us six months to live".
[
38
]
In 1996, Huang laid off more than half of Nvidia's employees-reducing headcount from 100 to 40-and focused the company's remaining resources on developing a graphics accelerator product optimized for processing triangle primitives: the
RIVA 128
.
[
27
]
[
36
]
By the time the RIVA 128 was released in August 1997, Nvidia had only enough money left for one month's payroll.
[
27
]
The sense of impending failure became so pervasive that it gave rise to Nvidia's unofficial company motto: "Our company is thirty days from going out of business."
[
27
]
Huang began internal presentations to Nvidia staff with those words for many years.
[
27
]
Nvidia sold about a million RIVA 128 units within four months,
[
27
]
and used the revenue to fund development of its next generation of products.
[
36
]
In 1998, the release of the
RIVA TNT
helped solidify Nvidia's reputation as a leader in graphics technology.
[
39
]
Public company
[
edit
]
Nvidia went public on January 22, 1999.
[
40
]
[
41
]
[
42
]
Investing in Nvidia after it had already failed to deliver on its contract turned out to be Irimajiri's best decision as Sega's president. After Irimajiri left Sega in 2000, Sega sold its Nvidia stock for $15 million.
[
38
]
In late 1999, Nvidia released the
GeForce 256
(NV10), its first product expressly marketed as a GPU, which was most notable for introducing onboard
transformation and lighting
(T&L) to consumer-level 3D hardware. Running at 120 MHz and featuring four-pixel pipelines, it implemented advanced video acceleration,
motion compensation
, and hardware sub-picture
alpha blending
. The GeForce outperformed existing products by a wide margin.
Because its products were performing well, Nvidia won the contract to develop the graphics hardware for Microsoft's Xbox game console, which included a $200 million advance. However, the project took many of its best engineers away from other projects. In the short term this did not matter, and the
GeForce 2 GTS
shipped in the summer of 2000. In December 2000, Nvidia reached an agreement to acquire the intellectual assets of its one-time rival
3dfx
, a pioneer in consumer 3D graphics technology leading the field from the mid-1990s until 2000.
[
43
]
[
44
]
The acquisition process was finalized in April 2002.
[
45
]
In 2001,
Standard & Poor's
selected Nvidia to replace the departing
Enron
in the S&P 500 stock index, meaning that index funds would need to hold Nvidia shares going forward.
[
46
]
In July 2002, Nvidia acquired
Exluna
for an undisclosed sum. Exluna made software-rendering tools and its personnel were merged into Nvidia's
Cg project
.
[
47
]
In August 2003, Nvidia acquired MediaQ for approximately US$70 million.
[
48
]
It launched
GoForce
the following year. On April 22, 2004, Nvidia acquired iReady, also a provider of high-performance
TCP offload engines
and
iSCSI
controllers.
[
49
]
In December 2004, it was announced that Nvidia would assist
Sony
with the design of the graphics processor (
RSX
) for the
PlayStation 3
game console. On December 14, 2005, Nvidia acquired
ULI Electronics
, which at the time supplied third-party
southbridge
parts for
chipsets
to
ATI
, Nvidia's competitor.
[
50
]
In March 2006, Nvidia acquired
Hybrid Graphics
.
[
51
]
